title: Never strand downstream protected website/Portal V2 releases after a provider-applied migration becomes source-merged
root_cause: Original protected #5648 applied and merged production blog handoff migration 20261112140500 but original provider-backed source lock remained at 827 although production ledger reached 828, repeating predecessor #5646→#5647 parity drift and blocking #5644.
impact: Whole protected release queue can stall, despite successful portal/browser tests; original production database remains healthy.
fix: Append exact production provider-applied version/name to original migration-history.lock.json in protected original migration lane, retaining previous 827 identities and full SQL source; never rerun applied DDL, mutate provider ledger or bypass Required/CodeQL.
prevention_rule: Original migration delivery owner must atomically hand off verified applied migration identity and provider readback to original lock source updater and downstream guarded CI before candidate consumers advance; detect 827→828 drift, preserve idempotent correlation/owner/ACK and keep obligations OPEN until processed; do not create a parallel scheduler.
evidence: Production provider 2026-11-12T13:41:02.290Z: 828 applied rows including exactly one 20261112140500/original_blog_provider_identity_handoff_v1
Original main #5648 includes SQL source, lock source at 827, #5644 protected dependency pending
Original provider-owned release ensures no fake migration status; exact protected CI and provider readback remain required.
outcome: Source lock parity candidate pending protected checks and independent 828/828 readback; tenant/consumer handoffs and actual app live still separately due.
